agent_priors_used: GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): when multiple independent agent lanes fail within minutes with the identical error signature (same model id, same exit code, same fingerprint, same control revision), the shared component, not the lanes' science, is the cause; repair the component once at the control plane instead of re-deriving new directions from the failures.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): a retryable execution failure (exit 75) that carries no output is an operational event, not evidence; a frozen experiment must be allowed to complete before any redirection is considered.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): prompt specification and model capability are separate failure modes; a 0/N result under an underspecified prompt cannot be attributed to capability until the specification variable is directly tested.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): a benchmark whose baselines sit at the ceiling has zero dynamic range and cannot detect a treatment effect even if the treatment is good - ceiling baselines are a null instrument, not weak evidence.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): continuing a mature thread is correct when the next result can still change an important architecture or product decision; and pre-freeze design-satisfiability failures (unsatisfiable gates, empty sampling frames, absent certificates) should be fixed once through the design-contract protocol rather than re-purchased cycle after cycle.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): long-lived research agents over-exploit their deepest local thread; a Global Director should prefer removing one shared blocker once over letting each lane re-discover the same absence.
